newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says 96/97 foundation for better result.
newsitem.headline: BHP says 96/97 foundation for better result.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday that its results for the year to May 31, 1997 laid the foundation for better results in the future.

BHP, Australia's largest listed company, earlier reported a 60.8 percent slump in year net profit to A$410 million after net abnormal losses of A$976 million, most of which were due to write-downs on underperforming assets.
"I am confident we are laying the foundation for a better result going forward," BHP managing director John Prescott told reporters.
"We are determined to do better than what we have done in this particular year and I think we have laid the foundation for doing so," Prescott said.

In its annual results, BHP wrote down the value of its North American copper assets by A$550 million, steel assets by A$220 million, minerals assets by A$189 million and petroleum assets by A$124 million.
The writedown of petroleum refinery assets was largely offset by the previously announced abnormal profit of A$107 million from the settlement of a tax dispute with the Victorian state government.
BHP's pre-abnormal profits rose A$93 million to A$1.386 billion, compared with analysts forecasts of between A$1.35 billion to A$1.4 billion.
